answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before it can trade meadow seed, jade, or basalt. Each identity gets the same transaction quota, so extra aliases require extra bonds. An attacker seeking 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds for the full period, even if the identities remain idle. This makes a sybil swarm costly in capital and lost interest, though a wealthy attacker can still pay.
